knowledge:
- key_parameters: lambda=adjusts the relative level of tumor burden in CancerDetector (default 0.5) ;; numTissues=positive integer representing the number of tissue types to classify reads into in cfDeconvolve ;; emAlgorithmType=type of EM algorithm to use in cfDeconvolve, options are "em.global.unknown" (default), "em.global.known", "em.local.unknown", "em.local.known" ;; likelihoodRatioThreshold=positive float threshold for filtering reads in cfDeconvolve (suggested/default is 2) ;; emMaxIterations=maximum iteration number for the EM algorithm in cfDeconvolve (default 100) ;; randomSeed=random seed to initialize the EM algorithm in cfDeconvolve (default 0) ;; id=unique sample ID string used in CancerDetector, cfDeconvolve, and cfSort
- alternatives: cfSort() is a supervised deep learning-based tissue deconvolution method for 29 major human tissues, whereas cfDeconvolve() is an EM-based deconvolution method for custom tissue types (> 2 classes)
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing cell-free DNA (cfDNA) bisulfite sequencing data to sensitively detect tumor-derived cfDNA or to deconvolve the tissue-of-origin composition of plasma samples
- pitfalls: In GenerateMarkerParam(), parameter values of NA:NA or 0:0 in the output list may cause errors in downstream analyses and must be removed before using the file ;; For cfSort(), the input markerName column must be obtained by intersecting the fragment-level methylation states with the specific cfSort marker file using hg19 genomic coordinates, using the region_index column as the markerName

workflows.name: cfdna_data_preparation
workflows.intent: Preprocess aligned paired-end reads and Bismark methylation extractor outputs to generate fragment-level methylation states and calculate marker beta distribution parameters.
input: demo.sorted.bed.txt.gz (sorted BED file of paired-end sequencing reads)
CpG_OT_demo.txt.gz (Bismark methylation extractor OT strand file)
CpG_OB_demo.txt.gz (Bismark methylation extractor OB strand file)
workflows.stages: 1. Merge paired-end sequencing reads to fragment-level using MergePEReads ;; 2. Merge CpG methylation states from top and bottom strands using MergeCpGs ;; 3. Combine fragment and methylation information using GenerateFragMeth ;; 4. Calculate paired shape parameters of beta distributions for markers using GenerateMarkerParam
workflows.code:
library(cfTools)
library(utils)
demo.dir <- system.file("data", package="cfTools")
PEReads <- file.path(demo.dir, "demo.sorted.bed.txt.gz")
head(read.table(PEReads, header=FALSE), 2)
fragInfo <- MergePEReads(PEReads)
head(fragInfo, 2)
CpG_OT <- file.path(demo.dir, "CpG_OT_demo.txt.gz")
CpG_OB <- file.path(demo.dir, "CpG_OB_demo.txt.gz")
head(read.table(CpG_OT, header=FALSE), 2)
head(read.table(CpG_OB, header=FALSE), 2)
methInfo <- MergeCpGs(CpG_OT, CpG_OB)
head(methInfo, 2)
fragMeth <- GenerateFragMeth(fragInfo, methInfo)
head(fragMeth, 2)
methLevel <- read.table(file.path(demo.dir, "beta_matrix.txt.gz"), 
                      row.names=1, header = TRUE)
sampleTypes <- read.table(file.path(demo.dir, "sample_type.txt.gz"), 
                        row.names=1, header = TRUE)$sampleType
markerNames <- read.table(file.path(demo.dir, "marker_index.txt.gz"), 
                        row.names=1, header = TRUE)$markerIndex
print(methLevel)
print(sampleTypes)
print(markerNames)
markerParam <- GenerateMarkerParam(methLevel, sampleTypes, markerNames)
print(markerParam)

workflows.name: cancer_detection
workflows.intent: Detect tumor-derived cfDNA fragments, estimate tumor burden, and visualize the resulting fractions.
input: CancerDetector.reads.txt.gz (fragment-level methylation states of reads mapped to cancer-specific markers)
CancerDetector.markers.txt.gz (paired shape parameters of beta distributions for cancer-specific markers)
workflows.stages: 1. Run CancerDetector to estimate tumor burden and normal cfDNA fraction ;; 2. Visualize the estimated fractions using PlotFractionPie
workflows.code:
fragMethFile <- file.path(demo.dir, "CancerDetector.reads.txt.gz")
markerParamFile <- file.path(demo.dir, "CancerDetector.markers.txt.gz")
head(read.csv(fragMethFile, sep = "\t", colClasses = "character"), 4)
head(read.csv(markerParamFile, sep = "\t"), 4)
CancerDetector(fragMethFile, markerParamFile, lambda=0.5, id="test")
cancer_normal_df <- CancerDetector(fragMethFile, markerParamFile, lambda=0.5, id="test")
PlotFractionPie(cancer_normal_df, title = "cfDNA Composition", class_colors = c("normal_cfDNA_fraction" = "blue"), font_size = 1.2)

workflows.name: tissue_deconvolution_em
workflows.intent: Estimate fractions of cfDNA fragments from different tissues using an EM algorithm.
input: cfDeconvolve.reads.txt.gz (fragment-level methylation states of reads mapped to tissue-specific markers)
cfDeconvolve.markers.txt.gz (paired shape parameters of beta distributions for tissue-specific markers)
workflows.stages: 1. Define EM algorithm parameters ;; 2. Run cfDeconvolve to estimate tissue fractions and unknown class fraction
workflows.code:
fragMethFile2 <- file.path(demo.dir, "cfDeconvolve.reads.txt.gz")
markerParamFile2 <- file.path(demo.dir, "cfDeconvolve.markers.txt.gz")
head(read.csv(fragMethFile2, header=TRUE, sep="\t", 
              colClasses = "character"), 4)
head(read.csv(markerParamFile2, header=TRUE, sep="\t", 
              colClasses = "character"), 4)
numTissues <- 7
emAlgorithmType <- "em.global.unknown"
likelihoodRatioThreshold <- 2
emMaxIterations <- 100
randomSeed <- 0
id <- "test"
tissueFraction <- cfDeconvolve(fragMethFile2, markerParamFile2, numTissues, 
                               emAlgorithmType, likelihoodRatioThreshold, 
                               emMaxIterations, randomSeed, id)
tissueFraction

workflows.name: tissue_deconvolution_cfsort
workflows.intent: Estimate fractions of cfDNA fragments derived from 29 major human tissues using a supervised deep learning model.
input: cfsort_reads.txt.gz (fragment-level methylation states of reads mapped to cfSort markers)
workflows.stages: 1. Run cfSort to estimate fractions across 29 tissue types
workflows.code:
fragMethInfo <- file.path(demo.dir, "cfsort_reads.txt.gz")
head(read.csv(fragMethInfo, header=TRUE, sep="\t", 
              colClasses = "character"), 4)
tissueFraction2 <- cfSort(fragMethInfo, id="demo")
tissueFraction2
